- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model exhibits mean reversion bias; align forecast toward recent 7–14 day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates in early period (first 5–7 days); cap initial forecast at +2% above recent 14-day moving average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating +/–), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% lag correction to forecast.
- When sentiment is consistently positive but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
